title: Phase recognition in SEM-EDX chemical maps using positive matrix factorization
author: Kong, Staničić, et al.

steps.title: Embed and polish particles
steps.instruction: Immobilize particles (100–200 µm) obtained from a 115 MWth CFB boiler in an epoxy‑hardener mixture, cure the resin, then polish stepwise to produce a flat surface that exposes the particle cross‑section.

steps.title: Acquire SEM‑EDX chemical maps
steps.instruction: Image the polished cross‑sections using a Quanta 200 ESEM FEG (FEI) equipped with an Oxford EDX system, recording elemental maps for the relevant elements (e.g., Fe, Ti, Si, Al, K, Na, Ca, P, S).

steps.title: Verify image contrast
steps.instruction: Confirm that the acquired images have sufficient contrast; do not raise brightness to the maximum, as this reduces contrast and can alter the PMF outcome. Adjust brightness only if contrast is preserved.

steps.title: Digitize image to vectors
steps.instruction: If the chemical map is a graphic file (e.g., PNG named “S1_Al.png”), use MATLAB to: (1) read the image with imread; (2) extract each RGB channel with im2double (S1_Al_1, S1_Al_2, S1_Al_3); (3) reshape each 2‑D matrix to a 1‑D column vector with reshape and transpose; (4) write each vector to a file using writematrix.

steps.title: Choose strongest color vector
steps.instruction: Inspect the three RGB vectors and select the one with the highest signal intensity; for purple images either the red or blue vector works, for black‑and‑white any vector is suitable, and this selection step can be omitted for already digital images.

steps.title: Assemble PMF input file
steps.instruction: Combine the selected element vectors into a single .txt, .csv, or .xls file where columns represent elements and rows represent pixel positions; optionally normalize each column so its maximum equals 1, and add an uncertainty column (use 1 % as in this study).

steps.title: Run EPA PMF analysis
steps.instruction: Load the concentration and uncertainty files into the open‑source EPA PMF program, set the number of runs (default 20) and the desired number of factors, execute the analysis, and export the “Profile” and “Contributions” sheets as the primary results.
